Extract one candidate view from a grid fit

Source: R/candidate-fit.R
candidate_fit.Rd

candidate_fit() turns one row of a grid-mode fit into a scalar-fit view. The returned object has the same class as object, with primary estimates and standard errors taken from object$tuning_grid, candidate-dependent extras such as W, ess, and neighbors rebuilt from cached ranks when the parent carried them, and candidate-independent state carried over. The rebuilt neighbors extra is the first k nearest observations, not the full DNN weight support.

Usage

candidate_fit(object, candidate, ...)

# Default S3 method
candidate_fit(object, candidate, ...)

# S3 method for class 'rdistnn_np_result'
candidate_fit(object, candidate, ...)

# S3 method for class 'rdistnn_cate_result'
candidate_fit(object, candidate, ...)

# S3 method for class 'rdistnn_affine_ratio_result'
candidate_fit(object, candidate, ...)

# S3 method for class 'rdistnn_plqr_result'
candidate_fit(object, candidate, ...)

candidate_fits(object, candidates = "all", ...)

# Default S3 method
candidate_fits(object, candidates = "all", ...)

# S3 method for class 'rdistnn_np_result'
candidate_fits(object, candidates = "all", ...)

# S3 method for class 'rdistnn_cate_result'
candidate_fits(object, candidates = "all", ...)

# S3 method for class 'rdistnn_affine_ratio_result'
candidate_fits(object, candidates = "all", ...)

# S3 method for class 'rdistnn_plqr_result'
candidate_fits(object, candidates = "all", ...)

Arguments

object

A grid fit returned by np_dnn(), cate_dnn(), or clate_dnn(), affine_ratio_dnn() or plqr_dnn() with tuning_mode = "grid".

candidate

A single candidate_id string or integer row index into object$tuning_grid$candidates.

...

Reserved for future methods.

candidates

"all" (default), a character vector of candidate ids, or an integer vector of candidate row indices.

Value

A scalar-style view with the same class as the parent. Affine-ratio views rebuild paired components and covariance from retained signals and frozen ranks; nuisance models and geometry are never refitted.

A named list of scalar-style candidate views.

Details

Reconstructed weights use cached ranks and target-specific distance groups, averaging within exact-distance blocks as in weights_matrix(). Candidate uncertainty redistributes each deleted member's block mass over the survivors using the n-1 rank table. Calls with ties warn once: the accompanying theory assumes a continuous distance distribution and does not establish inference under persistent ties. During experimental development, refit saved models after package updates.

Candidate IDs identify grid rows, not unique values of s. Repeated resolved orders remain separate candidates, and plots distinguish their IDs in labels. Extraction validates retained controls, target IDs and cached ranks; an incomplete or inconsistent saved object must be refitted.

Experimental methods

Methods for rdistnn_plqr_result objects are experimental, as is all PLQR functionality in this release; see plqr_dnn().

Examples

set.seed(1)
x_mat <- matrix(rnorm(40 * 2), 40, 2)
y_vec <- x_mat[, 1] + rnorm(40, sd = 0.2)
fit <- np_dnn(
  X = x_mat, x0 = c(0, 0), Y = y_vec,
  tuning_mode = "grid", se = FALSE
)
candidate_fit(fit, fit$tuning_grid$candidates$candidate_id[[1L]])
#> <rdistnn_np_result>
#>   localization: s = 4, s/n = 0.1
#>   data  : n=40, p=2, m=1
#>   DNN   : method=exact, k=1, distance=l2
#>   est   : mu[1:min(5,m)] = 0.0386  (SEs not requested)
